summary: Ars Technica reports on Google's AI additions to the Play Store: Ask Play expanding from per-listing Q&A to general app and game search with generated recommendations and comparison charts, a new Game Finder with a 'Gamer DNA' profile built from Android usage data, and a promised way to privately host and share personal vibe-coded apps. The excerpt covers discovery features in detail but says little about the private hosting feature beyond the headline and intro.
speakers_or_authors: Ars Technica staff writer (byline not shown in the item); Google is the source of the announcements.
relevance_reason: This is a vendor announcement of AI search and recommendation inside an app store, with a personal-data angle (usage data profiling). It is only loosely tied to the brief's themes of agents, personal context, voice, or OS-level AI. The private hosting of vibe-coded apps could matter, but the provided text gives no detail, and there is no hands-on evidence.
themes: AI built into app stores and devices
Conversational search versus browsing and lists

claims.claim: Ask Play is expanding from per-listing Q&A to a general conversational search for apps and games, generating recommendations that can include comparison charts. Gemini will get a similar capability later.
claims.quote: You ask the robot questions, and it generates recommendations that can include detailed comparison charts. Gemini will roll out a similar capability soon.

claims.claim: Google's Game Finder builds a 'Gamer DNA' profile from Android usage data covering 1.2 billion players and matches users with similar players. Users can tune it by rating games.
claims.quote: featuring insights into the way 1.2 billion people play games on Android. It builds a profile called Gamer DNA and matches you with players who have similar DNA.

claims.claim: The Play Store will soon let people privately host and share apps they built with AI. No details are given on how it works or when it ships.
claims.quote: the Play Store will soon offer a way to privately host and share those creations.

claims.claim: Prompting Game Finder with specific preferences is promised for later. How much customization exists at launch is unclear, and the accuracy gain from rating games is unverified.
claims.quote: Google says you’ll eventually be able to prompt Game Finder with fairly specific game preferences, but it’s unclear how much customization will be available at launch.

claims.claim: Game Finder and Gamer DNA roll out in the US on the day of the article, with other markets to follow.
claims.quote: Game Finder and Gamer DNA are rolling out in the US today, with other markets following “soon.”

commercial_interest: Vendor announcement: the claims come from Google about its own Play Store products. The article offers no independent testing or user reports.
older_event: No. These are new announcements as of the publication date (2026-10-13). Ask Play itself launched in 2025, and this is its expansion.
